drug_class: Amylin analog (a synthetic hormone that helps control blood sugar)
purpose: Pramlintide is used along with insulin to help control blood sugar levels in people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. It is not a replacement for insulin — it works alongside your insulin to improve blood sugar control, especially after meals. It can also help reduce appetite and may support modest weight loss.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes a hormone called amylin alongside insulin, but in people with diabetes this hormone is often missing or not working well. Pramlintide acts like that missing hormone. It helps by slowing down how fast food leaves your stomach, preventing your liver from releasing too much sugar after meals, and helping you feel full sooner so you eat less.
common_side_effects: Nausea is the most common side effect, especially when you first start using it — this often gets better over time. You may also experience vomiting, stomach pain, or loss of appetite. Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) is a serious risk, especially when used with insulin, so watch for shakiness, sweating, dizziness, or confusion.
warnings: Never mix pramlintide in the same syringe as insulin — they must be given as separate injections. Because it can cause low blood sugar, your doctor will likely lower your insulin dose when you start this medication. Do not use it if you cannot feel the signs of low blood sugar (called hypoglycemia unawareness). Always carry a fast-acting sugar source with you in case your blood sugar drops too low.
typical_dosing: For type 2 diabetes, the starting dose is usually 60 micrograms injected just under the skin right before major meals. For type 1 diabetes, the starting dose is typically 15 micrograms before meals. Your doctor will slowly increase your dose based on how well you tolerate it. It is injected in the stomach area or thigh — not the same spot as your insulin injection.
